newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Liberia's Taylor escapes assassination attempt.
newsitem.headline: Liberia's Taylor escapes assassination attempt.

text.p: Liberia's chief warlord Charles Taylor said he survived an assassination attempt on Thursday when gunmen ambushed him inside the presidential palace.

Taylor's senior aide was killed in the commando-style attack by gunmen who forced their way into the Executive Mansion in jeeps. Panic gripped the capital Monrovia which is still recovering from devastating ethnic warfare in April and May.
African peacekeepers trying to end nearly seven years of civil war in the West African country quickly moved in with tanks and deployed across the city's commercial district.
Radio reports said 10 people died in the attack.
Taylor, who started Liberia's civil war in 1989 but is now a member of the interim ruling council, described the attack in a broadcast on his Kiss FM radio.

"As I entered the sixth floor of the Executive Mansion I came under a hail of fire in which my senior aide-de-camp Jackson Manley and my ECOMOG (military) aide-de-camp and several of my senior staff were wounded," he added.
"I was not hit, through the mercy of God," he said.

Taylor did not say who could have carried out the attack. Last April his forces spearheaded attempts to arrest ethnic Krahn warlord Roosevelt Johnson, a rival. The resulting all-out warfare devasted the capital Monrovia and derailed a delicate regional accord on ending the civil war.

The city was devastated by looting and the United States military evacuated foreigners and sent Marines and ships to protect its embassy. Liberia was founded by freed American slaves in 1847 and has traditional links with the United States.

A witness who was near the Executive Mansion said the unidentified attackers overran a checkpoint at the entrance to the mansion, which is guarded by troops of the Nigerian-led ECOMOG West African peacekeeping force stationed in Liberia.

"There was an attack on the mansion and shooting broke out," one witness said. "Shops, businesses, markets and schools closed hurriedly and traffic came to a halt. People started running... some with their belongings."

At least two wounded were taken to the nearby Barclay Training Centre army barracks, witnesses said. BTC was the bastion of ethnic Krahn guerrillas at the heart of militia warfare in the capital six months ago.
The attack happened only three days after ECOMOG began to deploy across the country in earnest to start disarming guerrillas under a new peace deal.

The warfare in April and May blew off course a 1995 accord which was believed to be the most promising because all the main faction leaders signed it and were given jobs. A dozen earlier ones failed to end fighting which has killed more than 150,000 people and devastated the economy and infrastructure.
Taylor asked his National Patriotic Front of Liberia fighters to stay calm and demobilised and ECOMOG to take charge.

He said he did not expect the attack to affect the latest peace signed last August setting a new disarmemnt timetable and elections for next May. Taylor has already declared he will run for president.
